title: Alpargatas 2026 Q3 Earnings Call
contentEn:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for waiting.

Welcome to Alpargatas' Third Quarter 2026 Results Webcast.

[Operator Instructions] If you are listening to me, this is Joao, and I'm going to be your interpreter for today.

[Operator Instructions] Please be advised that this webcast is being recorded and will be made available on the company's IR, Investor Relations website, ri.alpargatas.com.br, where the complete material from our earnings release is available.

The presentation can also be downloaded via the chat icon, including in English.

[Operator Instructions] We advise that all questions be asked at once.

We would like to point out that the information contained in this presentation and any statements that may be made during this webcast regarding Alpargatas' business outlook, projections and operating and financial targets constitute beliefs and assumptions of the company's management as well as information currently available.

Forward-looking statements are not guarantees of performance.

They involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions as they relate to future events and therefore, depend on circumstances that may or may not occur.

Investors should understand that general economic conditions, market conditions and other operating factors may affect Alpargatas' future performance and lead to results that differ materially from those expressed in such forward-looking statements.

Joining us today are the company's executives, Mr. Liel Miranda, CEO; Mr. Andre Natal, CFO and Investor Relations Officer; and Ms. Melina Rodrigues, Investor Relations Director.

I'll now turn the floor over to Mr. Liel.

Good morning, everyone.

It's a big pleasure to be with you today about our third quarter's results.

Before going on into each one of the pillars of our strategy, the overall message is that this was one more quarter that showed the consistency of our results, showing a positive variation, both for the top line and bottom lines.

I think this is an important thing because this reflects our growth strategy, both in our revenue and growth and sales, but also on our margins.

So it's not a strategy that focus on one or another variation or indicators, but it's a strategy focused on both the top and the bottom lines.

Another one is that -- another important thing is that we have a variation in this third quarter where we see that all of our business units in all geographies are growing or are showing growth, and that's important because we went through a phase where the improvement was the operational improvement, much more focused in cost control and internal efficiency.

We went through a phase where we try to -- we made the Brazil business unit go back to growing.

Now the latest quarter shows that all of our geographies are ready to keep growing and increase our participation in all of our -- the priority markets where we operate in.

When we look at Brazil, the most important point is that we continue absolutely focused on our operational efficiency.

Our OTIF, on time in full metric keeps growing.

It's getting close to 85% right now.

And we have an excellent performance, both in the sales volume to our clients as well as to the sales volume sold from our clients to our consumers, growing 13% in the grocery channel and 10% in Havaianas' stores and overall growing about 8%.

So through that, we keep gaining market share.

And now we reached a growth of about -- market share of about 80%.

This is the only one where we can check our numbers, which is measured by Nielsen.

This shows the strength of the brand and the services we are showing to our clients, the service levels we are offering to our clients.

When we look internationally, all geographies show growth.

Europe continues to have a good performance since last year and growing again in this quarter, 17% in the first 9 months of 2026.

The United States geography in which we showed our business model last year, this is still the first year of the transition.

And we already see results in the growth in sell-in and sell-through, which is the sales of our distributor to its clients.

And in the distribution market, which goes from Latin America to Asia and Africa, we saw a recovery.

In the first half of the year, we saw a decrease in the volume compared to last year.

But now in the third quarter, we already see a regain of volume, especially in the priority markets in Asia and South -- for example, South Africa, which is a sign that our strength of brand and execution is good.

We also continue our market investments to be aligned to our strategy, gaining visibility to our brands and not only in Brazil, but internationally, which is our strategy.

For example, our participation in fashion weeks in Europe, which take place around this time in the year and are trendsetting for the summer next year.

Havaianas was present in all of those fashion weeks being a part of the trends that should be valid for next year.

And we realized that the segments where we would have a smaller market share and where we have been developing our portfolio and specific products for those lines, which is the men's and kids, we see a more accelerated growth than we see in the overall volume growth.

And last for this financial standpoint of view, we continue our financial discipline because it is an discipline -- growth and discipline.

And in this strategy, we keep reducing, managing our operational expenses, managing our cash consumption.

And mainly, we continue to see the evolution of our return on investment -- invested capital since a very low level about 3 years ago, and now we are already at 19%, which is a huge priority for us, keep evolving, so the ROIC continues evolving.

I think this gives you a good overall idea of the business, and now Andre is going to go through each one of the aspects.

Good morning, everyone.

It's a pleasure to be with you.

As Liel said, we had a quarter, which was very important from the perspective of growth.

In this quarter, we grew in all the operations in all geographies where we operate in, especially looking at the expansion of the international markets.

As Liel said, it was the third wave of this journey that we were pursuing.

And right now, we can see a good expansion -- double-digit expansion in our priority geographies and all.

So, a certain stabilization of the operations in the market supported by -- through distribution, which is the IDM market, where we wanted to reduce the volatility in those operations.

When we look at the U.S., particularly, you know that we have changed the business model about a year ago, and this turnaround is taking us -- this change is taking us to a very interesting performance of the expansion of doors we serve and also the expansion and therefore, the expansion of volume, which is important for the scale of this operation.

There, we saw a growth of 82% in this third quarter.

Europe had already shown in the first half of the year a double-digit growth, and we kept this traction now in the third quarter where there is a smaller seasonality after summer.

But yet we grew 13% in Europe.

So as I said, the geographies supported by -- through distributions, which is Latin America, Asia and Australia, this is a very expense and diverse geographies, but we think the stabilization of the business there is very important.

So, we can create the foundations to have a more robust growth in those regions, too.

And although Brazil who is a big part of the business, considering -- because of the size of its sales compared to the overall sales volume, in there, in Brazil, we grew 7%, which shows that we have also interesting traction with our consumers.

So, there is no big movements of stock-out in the channels or stock-out in our supply chain or in retailers.

There is a very strong focus within the company of -- in fact, accelerating the demand at the edge with the consumers, which is going to show how healthy our growth is.

On next slide, we already see a longer year-to-date overview with very close figures, very similar figures.

53% of growth in the American operation, 18% in U.S.A. which is also an interesting growth and aligned with the double-digit performance, sell-out performances across geographies in Europe.

And also in a longer window time, we see that the IDM has also shown a more stable -- showing that we have reduced the volatility in those markets, and we have a decrease of about 1% in these year-to-date results.

We think that in this moment, the connection of sell-in and sell-out is more effective right now.

And again, in Brazil, Brazil's results shows that this trend of 7% to 8%, which has been seen in the last 3 quarters is a growth that seems interesting given the size of our geography and given the size of the penetration we have in the industry and also the market share in this geography. yet we are growing 8% every quarter.

So, overall growth of 8%, a 12% growth in our revenue.

This is the year-to-date figure.

And we see these results in the cash generation.

We saw one more quarter of cash generation, which was good, about BRL 150 million.

This is connected to this expansion of all the operations, expanding the gross margins as I'm going to show later on in this presentation.

And this has been showing us to gain more efficiency in our operations and gain more scale as well.

As for the leverage or indebtedness level from the cash generation, we saw once again a deleveraging of the company, which has been continuous.

If you look at the graph on the right-hand side, we have been deleveraging or reducing the debt of the company.

We made a reduction of capital and dividends also to go back to some indebtedness.

Again, gradually, it has been decreasing due to the cash generation we have had.

So, we reached 0.3x the EBITDA.

So now about our working capital variation.

We had a little bit of a consumption of working capital, about BRL 39 million, about BRL 6 million less compared to the third quarter last year, but this is without expanding the time line.

The time lines are regular compared to the previous quarter.

Actually, in a few quarters, we have had the same time line of working capital cash.

When you look at the bars for the last 4 quarters, we see that this cash consumption -- about 80% of this variation is explained by the growth of the operation.

So naturally, as we have good performance for sell-out and good performance of sell-in growth across all geographies, naturally, this is going to demand more stock, more receivables.

So as the line graph can see, we are not deteriorating our time frame for the receivables and for our stocks.

So therefore, our operations stabilized, and we are seeing a growth level that demands some capital consumption, which is completely normal because of the -- again, for the growth of our operation.

On the right-hand side, we see the investment levels, which are also showing quite similar in the past 2 years when quarterly analyzed.

It accelerates throughout the quarters in the year as we deploy our projects mapped, and it's totally within the limits that have been improved in our capital allocation in our last meeting.

So again, this is inside a normal cycle as well as in accordance with the seasonality of these investments as had been defined.

Moving on to the seasonality of Brazil.

Brazil saw a sell-in 7% growth, which is compared to the 8% of the sell-out growth.

So, you see that the sell-out grew a little bit more than the sell-in this quarter, which also reaffirms what we have been saying for quite a while, the importance of not making large stock-out in our channels.

The obsession now we have is the obsession now of keeping accelerated sell-out and this naturally will demand our sell-in increase as the stocks must be replenished.

When we look at the right-hand graph, we see an accumulation of about 7 million pairs of stock-out in this quarter.

This is compatible to the seasonal movements where the retailers are stocking out, so they prepare for the summer in Brazil.

So, these stock levels are aligned with the past years and it's needed in the market to be supplied properly for the upcoming summer.

And we can see the last 12 months' variation.

There was a small, about 1.9 million pairs added to the stock-out.

Obviously, this is estimative because the sell-out is based on estimate of data that we have access to.

But either way, this is a movement that shows a connection -- a very strong connection between the sell-in and sell-out in long window times.

In quarterly windows, this changes a little bit because of the seasonality.

But in the long time line, what we are always pursuing is this.

Remember that as the operation and the sales grow, also the numbers of stock in the chain should also grow, but they shouldn't be exactly identical, but they should be -- they should allow the stock-out to grow as the demand for the category grows in the retail or in the market.

Moving on.

Now, we see the expansion of our gross margin.

I think the line in the graph speaks for themselves.

This shows how much the gross margin has been expanding over time, has reached now 50%.

I think this is the best number we have ever had in the third quarter in a very long time, at least to say the least, but we can see this evolution -- this large evolution.

Despite the fact, in Brazil, we have not yet grown -- regrown completely the scale we used to have in 2021.

So this margin -- gross margin expansion has been precisely from the efficiency gains.

Of course, in the past few years, we have also recovered some volume, but this is due to the better efficiency.

On this slide now, we see our SG&A.

It's broken down in 3 components.

There is a main component of evolution -- quarterly evolution, which is the marketing, which is the dark green line.

There, we see an evolution, which is back to 6% of our revenue.

This was already expected.

We remind everyone that in the third quarter of 2025, we had seen investment levels, which was a little bit smaller than the average for the year.

And this gave us a little bit more of an expansion of EBITDA margin, which you can see on the right-hand side graph was of 30% of EBITDA margin, but that was because of that specific time window.

We explained that we don't manage the marketing account every quarter.

We do it based on the calendar for activation -- marketing activations, which are necessary and defined at the beginning of the year.

So, we officially had a slower -- a lower marketing expenditure, and now we are back to this level of 6%.

When we look especially at the fixed expenses, we can see some negative evolution in the growth of expenses.

And this is due to a series of factors within the company.

There is one factor that has different basis to the previous one, which is the payroll tax reinstatement.

This explains about 20% of this variation.

We also had some one-time off like market pricing of our long-term incentives, which is again related to the payroll tax reinstatement.

And also once our shares -- share price goes up and this has been performing well, we also bring some correction of all the provisions made for these long time incentive programs that need to be taken.

These provisions need to be increased.

And this can go up and down according to the performance of the stock prices.

We also have seen sales of energy and other products that were smaller, which also has an effect on the comparison basis -- unfavorable compared to the comparison basis.

None of them is big enough, but all of them together lead to this amount of about -- and when we see the right-hand side graph, when we look at the EBITDA margin, right now, we are already, as I said before, we have a smaller scale compared to 5 years ago.

We already have a larger EBITDA compared to the third quarter in 2025 when we had seen a market investment that was much smaller.

And now on this slide, we see the international market's evolution.

We also saw a volume evolution of about 15%, considering all the geographies outside Brazil, which is important because in the sense of our regaining of scale and also because we understand the international market as an avenue for growth because of its opportunity size, because of the size of the opportunity and also because of the symptoms that we are growing across all geographies.

This makes us excited and makes us believe that finally, we might be making this potential to materialize.

When you look at the revenues on the left column of this table, we see an evolution on the revenue per pair of about 80% in Europe and about 9% in the international distribution markets' MDI.

There was exchange rate, a little bit unfavorable result, which brought it a little bit down, but this is not only the evolution of price.

It's also a better mix of channel, mix of geographies, mix of products that are being sold there.

So, there is indeed a positive evolution of our mix.

And obviously, the exception is the U.S., where these numbers are due to the -- our revenue per pair are decreasing because we now have the intermediary in the chain, right, which is the Eastman resulting from this new business model.

So, this effect is also explained by this new business model.

Now moving on to the gross margin in the international.

We are growing again another 2 percentage points compared to -- in the revenue, which also comes -- arises from a better efficiency, but also gains in scale.

So, growth is still very important.

We now have a scale, which is bigger than we had in 2021, 2022, but we are getting very close to the gross margins that were obtained at the time, although we have a smaller scale right now.

So, what we have been growing now is our volume and regain the scale, although we are not there yet, on par with what we had in 2021, 2022.

Now looking at the marketing investment, the orange line.

We see a positive variation at a different level, smaller than we used to have in previous years, but which we believe to be absolutely normal and within what we expect for our operations abroad.

And also the evolution of fixed and variable expenses, we also see a favorable evolution.

Of course, there is here a lot of effect of the U.S.A.

This is the trade-off for the expressive results.

We reduced, both the expenses we had in U.S. because of the distribution model and also because of the headcount and office, and all kind of admin and warehousing expenses.

Now, all of them were direct expenses.

Now, they are operated by our business partner.

So, this helps us in this favorable evolution of our efficiency levels here.

And because of that, we reached a positive EBITDA margin, which we hadn't seen in the past 5 years in the third quarter.

So when we go a year back, only in the distribution market -- only distribution markets a year ago had positive EBITDA.

The margin in U.S.A. and Europe a year ago were negative.

And now we see that all the international regions are positively contributing -- are contributing with positive results to the EBITDA.

If we want to break it down this evolution a year from now, 50% of this evolution is due to the turnaround of profitability in the U.S. and 30% of the turnaround of the European business and 30% also profitability in the international distribution market.

So, all of the markets bringing this positive contribution that resulted in a positive EBITDA result for the overall international performance.

Moving on now.

We see Rothy's that is still growing its top line, which is sales, right, to the market or revenue, which is important because since they grow, they also have a decompression of scale.

They gain scale and they reduce the compression of margins.

They were affected this quarter, specifically because of logistics issues and higher freight prices.

So, we see here an unfavorable evolution, both in the gross margin and the EBITDA margin.

It reached an EBITDA of minus negative $2 million, subtracting from the last 12-month performance that we saw in the records of the company.

It was also affected by the tariffs imposed by the U.S.A. and some growth in the marketing expenses related to the autumn campaign that was launched.

This is the combination of all of those factors.

Despite the evolution of the top line, led to a contraction of the company's results.

I think these are the main points that we had to present to you.

And now we are going to open for Q&A if you have any questions.

summary: Alpargatas Q3 2026 net sales reached R$1.240 billion, up 11.1%, with adjusted EBITDA of R$283.5 million and a 22.9% margin. Brazil sell-out grew 8%, international volume increased 14.6%, U.S. volume grew 82%, and international operations delivered their first positive third-quarter EBITDA in five years. Rothy's sales increased 12% to US$51 million, while freight, tariffs, new stores and marketing resulted in negative US$2.2 million EBITDA.

highlights: Net sales increased 11.1% to R$1.240 billion
Adjusted EBITDA increased 10.9% to R$283.5 million
Brazil sell-out increased 8% and grocery market share reached 79.9%
U.S. volume increased 82% with no channel inventory accumulation
Rothy's sales increased 12% to US$51 million
revenueDrivers: Brazil consumer sell-out, disciplined channel replenishment, European growth, U.S. door expansion and recovery in priority distributor markets supported revenue.
marginDrivers: Manufacturing efficiency, scale, favorable mix and a leaner U.S. distributor model supported profitability; payroll-tax reinstatement and long-term-incentive remeasurement pressured fixed expenses, while freight, tariffs and store investment pressured Rothy's.
guidance: Management did not issue formal 2027 guidance. Capital and operating investments will be phased after consumer traction is validated and will undergo scenario-sensitivity and risk review.
risks: Brazil labor and tax reform, raw-material and FX volatility, channel inventory discipline, international execution, Rothy's freight and tariff pressure, and the timing of growth investments.
